questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should you still wear a seat belt?

options.text: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
No, seat belts are not needed.
Seat belts should only be worn in the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags are safety devices that help protect you in crashes. For the best protection, always wear your lap and shoulder belts together with airbags.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that you cannot turn in the direction shown by the arrow. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs mark areas where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: True or false: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk.
questions.explanation: Drivers must stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You must also yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on your side of the road when there are no traffic signals.

questions.question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press down hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Before stopping, check your mirrors to see traffic around you. Release the accelerator slowly, then move your foot to the brake pedal and press with steady pressure for a smooth stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn you about conditions ahead. This sign means a steep hill is coming. Slow down and be ready to shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: True or false: At a four-way stop, you must yield to drivers who arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to any driver who arrived before you. Wait your turn before entering the intersection.

questions.question: True or false: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road.
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Be careful around children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for animals, people, or bicycles that may cross the road.

questions.question: True or false: You must signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes. Signal in the direction you are moving.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a blizzard, you should stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If stranded in winter weather, stay with your vehicle. Run the engine only for short periods. Open a window to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that your road ends at an intersection ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop or turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead has curves and turns.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers to be careful when roads are wet. Wet pavement is slippery and harder to drive on safely.

questions.question: A bad suspension can cause:
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and keeps it comfortable on different road surfaces. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull off the road. Only pass on the right if you can do so without leaving the roadway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Last turn before a toll road.

questions.explanation: Orange signs mark work zones. When you see orange signs, cones, or barrels, stay alert for unexpected conditions. This sign warns of a flagger ahead. Obey the flagger's directions.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a traffic signal that is not working?

options.text: Stop completely and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop. Stop completely and look. Yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a reverse curve. The road curves right, then curves left.

questions.question: When must you slow down in a school zone?

options.text: On school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m., when children are present, and where signs are posted.

questions.correctAnswerText: On school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m., when children are present, and where signs are posted.
questions.explanation: Slow to 20 mph in school zones on school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m., when children are present, and where signs are posted.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right turns are allowed on a red light.

questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. You cannot turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on the road. You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign. Do not go until the intersection is clear and safe to cross.

questions.question: When turning right, should you let a bicyclist pass before making your turn if the bicyclist is approaching on the right?
questions.explanation: If you are turning right and a bicyclist is approaching on the right, let the bicyclist go through the intersection first before you turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The railroad crossing is controlled. Continue at your regular speed.
Look, listen, and be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Stop at the railroad tracks and wait for a signal before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. Wait for all trains to pass before you cross.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flag person is ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear orange or yellow vests and use paddles and flags to direct traffic through construction zones.

questions.question: Which of these substances can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. These include prescription drugs like tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter medicines like cough syrup and cold tablets, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: At a green light, should you look left and right before entering the intersection?
questions.explanation: Even when your light turns green, you must check for other vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection before you go.

questions.question: What are "no zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars cannot be seen or are too close for the truck driver to stop and turn safely.
Areas where cars have plenty of space behind the truck.
Areas where cars are several car lengths away from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars cannot be seen or are too close for the truck driver to stop and turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks and buses where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where cars are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or maneuver safely. Being in a "no zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?

options.text: The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers.

questions.explanation: A red painted curb means you cannot stop, stand, or park there.

questions.question: Must a crash report be filed if there is death, injury, or property damage over $1,500?
questions.explanation: A crash report must be filed if there is death, injury, or property damage over $1,500. If an uninsured vehicle is involved, a report must be filed for $500 or more in damage.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may proceed if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around if you are driving toward this sign.
